ios.desc:
Peek is the money app that doesn't lecture you. No spreadsheets, no guilt trips, no budgets you'll abandon by Tuesday.

Instead, Peek talks to you. It notices a charge, asks what happened, and helps you see the story behind your spending — the impulse TikTok buy, the Friday coffee ritual, the "while I'm here" spiral. Over time, it learns how you think about money and reflects it back so you actually understand your own patterns.

How it works:

Peek checks in with you about your recent spending through quick, casual conversations. It asks the right questions — not "did you stay under budget?" but "was that worth it to you?" — and builds a picture of your spending behavior that gets sharper over time.

What makes Peek different:

→ Conversations, not spreadsheets
→ Self-awareness, not restrictions
→ Understands your "why," not just your "what"
→ Built for how Gen Z actually relates to money

Peek won't tell you to stop buying oat milk. It'll help you notice that you buy it every time you're stressed — and let you decide what to do with that.

Your money. Your patterns. Your call.

quotes.text:
hey hn –

mint is gone, the clones feel like bloatware, and afaict every “personal finance” app still assumes you love staring at pie charts for fun. i don’t.

so i built peek.

- ai-first: an ai agent does the number-crunching and pings you with bite-sized nudges instead of guilt-trips

- habit loop > dashboard: get weekly “wrapped”-style digests that actually push you towards forming new positive habits, not just remind you you spent too much on coffee

- mobile-only rn (ios) bc that’s where gen z actually lives

link: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/peek-ai-personal-finance-app/id6742875016

would love honest feedback – performance, ux, skeptical takes, whatever. tear it apart. i’ll be here in the thread.
